headline: Hot Inflation Print Sends Stocks Lower as Rate-Hike Fears Take Over
body_html:
Wall Street retreated on Tuesday as a hot inflation reading and pointed comments from Federal Reserve officials pushed interest-rate worries to the front. Officials were reported to be open to a half-point rate increase. Of the 667 stocks we track, 423 fell and only 238 rose, a clearly negative tape.

The rotation followed the rate logic. Energy was the only sector to finish higher, up 0.25%. Homebuilders took the heaviest damage, down 3.47%, followed by financials at 2.53% lower and materials at 1.55% lower. Industrials, semiconductors and healthcare each slipped roughly 0.7%, while software lost 0.6% and consumer names gave up 0.42%.

The standout mover was AAON, the HVAC maker, which jumped 19.31% and ran against the market. Our headlines offered no explanation for the move. On the other side, Hims & Hers Health fell 16.52%, and Legend Biotech and Novanta each dropped more than 15%. With Wednesday, November 11 next, the market's attention stays on whether the Fed's hawkish tone hardens further.

briefs.headline: Fed Talk Turns Hawkish
briefs.body: Reports that policymakers are willing to consider a half-point rate increase, as inflation runs hotter, set the tone for the session. Traders have been raising their bets on a hike, and the shift weighed on the most rate-sensitive corners of the market.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders and Banks Lead the Slide
briefs.body: Homebuilders fell 3.47% and financials lost 2.53%, the two weakest sectors on the day. Both groups are sensitive to the path of borrowing costs, so the prospect of tighter policy hit them harder than the rest of the market.

briefs.headline: Energy Stands Alone in the Green
briefs.body: Energy was the only sector to close higher, rising 0.25%, while all eight others declined. The gain was modest, but in a session where more than 400 stocks fell, it was enough to make the group a relative bright spot.

briefs.headline: Software Splits Down the Middle
briefs.body: The software group slipped 0.6%, but the stock moves underneath were far wider. Zeta Global Holdings climbed 8.23%, while cybersecurity name Qualys tumbled 13.51%. Investors were picking winners and losers inside the sector rather than trading it as one block.

briefs.headline: Pump Prices Ease to a Four-Month Low
briefs.body: U.S. gasoline prices have dipped under a key psychological threshold for the first time since July. The relief at the pump offers households some breathing room, even as the inflation data and the Fed's reaction dominate the market conversation.

briefs.headline: Washington Keeps the Pressure on Iran
briefs.body: Secretary of State Rubio told G7 counterparts the U.S. will keep imposing heavy costs on Iran, and argued major combat operations are unnecessary given the economic campaign. Tehran's top security official said no talks with Washington are underway.
